prompt:
CONCEPT: a citizen of the Sodium Nation, of the Salt House. A female personification character with a salt pan — shallow white basins, a wooden rake, a windmill pump as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Sodium (Na) to carry in her design and the scene: a bright yellow flame that bursts when it touches water, cube-shaped salt crystals, the warm orange of sodium street lamps; soft silvery metal that must be kept under oil. Palette: sodium yellow, salt white, oil-dark silver, lamp orange.
HOUSE TRAITS of Salt: white cubic crystals, the white crust of a salt pan, coarse grain and sparkle; the gathered, nourishing side of salt. Palette: salt white, sea blue, sun gold, wood brown.
AGE: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
SILHOUETTE: toned athletic-curvy, full-busted with rounded hips build; a long ponytail with blunt straight bangs; cream-blonde hair.
FACE — she must read as her own person at a glance, NOT the style's default pretty face and not a sister of the other characters: first impression — a boyish, mischievous tomboy energy; deep brown skin; oval face; moderately sized, realistically proportioned eyes — soft droopy eyes, outer eye corners tilting sharply upward; thick straight brows; upturned nose; wide smiling mouth; sky-blue eyes; a bare, makeup-free face.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1880, a street of gas lamps and a soda works: salt pans, evaporating basins, a sodium lamp glowing orange, brass and white crust. COSTUME (citizen, steampunk): her object leads — its silhouette, parts and materials must read at first glance in her outfit and headpiece, the object reimagined as cloth, leather and brass fittings; the steampunk era only sets the late-Victorian cut and the brass-and-leather finish. Steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise. HAIR: her hair is worn exactly as SILHOUETTE says — loose, long or cut as named; do not pin it up into a bun or tuck it under goggles or a hat unless SILHOUETTE says an updo.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or a short hem where the outfit allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the object's shape, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
EXPRESSION: asymmetric grin with teeth just showing, one brow raised, eyes narrowed with amusement.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Na) and atomic number (11) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
